job.title: HSEQ Manager
job.description:
HSEQ Manager (OFSC)

Role Details
  • Location: North West Sydney
  • Employment type: Permanent, full-time
  • Salary range: Base + super (commensurate with experience)

Role Overview

We are seeking a HSEQ Manager specialising in build construction and OSFC related work to join a growing Tier 2 construction company.

My client is expanding at a significant rate due to a strong reputation and company culture encouraging good employee tenure. Retaining good people and strong supportive culture including HSEQ is key for the CEO and company mission.

The successful candidate will work with the executive team to develop, implement, and audit integrated management systems that meet certification and accreditation requirements. Filtering into a safe and well organised project team(s).


Key Responsibilities
  • Develop and implement HSEQ management systems aligned to ISO 45001, ISO 9001, ISO 14001, and the Office of the Federal Safety Commissioner (OFSC) Australian Government Building and Construction WHS Accreditation Scheme.
  • Conduct internal audits against ISO standards and the FSC Audit Criteria, including preparation of audit reports, findings, and corrective action recommendations.
  • Facilitate workshops to map business processes, identify gaps, and design system requirements that meet relevant standards and regulatory obligations.
  • Conduct site audits and safety inspections across client construction operations, including high-risk environments.
  • Develop tailored HSEQ strategies, frameworks, and improvement plans for construction clients.
  • HSEQ Operational duties as well as strategic direction dovetailing into won tenders and ongoing projects 
  • Provide ongoing advisory support to clients pursuing or maintaining certification and accreditation.
Essential Experience & Qualifications
  • 5–8 years' experience in HSEQ consulting, GRC, or in-house management systems roles within the construction industry.
  • Tertiary qualifications in WHS, Quality, Environmental Management, Engineering, or a related discipline.
  • Demonstrated working knowledge of ISO 45001 (OH&S), ISO 9001 (Quality), ISO 14001 (Environment), and OFSC WHS Accreditation Scheme.
  • Proven experience developing and implementing integrated management or uplifting existing systems for construction businesses.
  • Internal auditing experience against ISO standards (Lead Auditor qualification highly regarded).
  • Strong workshop facilitation and stakeholder engagement skills, including with senior client stakeholders.
  • Hands-on experience conducting site-based safety inspections and audits on active construction sites.
  • Working knowledge of the WHS Act and Regulation, relevant Codes of Practice, and construction-specific high-risk work requirements.
  • Excellent written communication — capable of producing audit reports, procedures, and strategy documents to a high professional standard.
Desirable
  • Lead Auditor certification (Exemplar Global or equivalent) for ISO 45001 / 9001 / 14001.
  • Experience working with Tier 1/2 builders.
  • White Card and any additional construction-related tickets/competencies.
  • Demonstrated ability to navigate and use construction tech platforms such as HammerTech, Procore, 1Breadcrumb, or similar HSEQ/site management systems.
  • Knowledge of additional frameworks (e.g. ISO 27001, ISO 55001) is a plus.
Candidate Profile

We're looking for a self-directed consultant with deep construction industry credibility and formal tertiary qualifications — someone who can run client engagements end-to-end, lead workshops with construction executives, write systems, and walk a site conducting audits in the same week.

Strong commercial acumen and the ability to translate compliance requirements into practical, business-friendly solutions is essential.

job.title: WHS Business Partner - Contract

Zenergy's contract and interim division is teaming up with a household-name Australian logistics operator to find a WHS Business Partner for their growing team. This is a 6-month contract supporting a business that moves fast — think warehouses, sorting hubs, delivery centres, and a sprawling network of drivers and contractors.

You'll report directly to the National WHS Manager, stepping into a role that's as strategic as it is hands-on. You'll be the trusted safety partner for operational leaders, frontline crews, and support teams alike — getting ahead of WHS risks, keeping the business compliant, and continuously raising the bar on safety performance.

What the Role Involves:
  • Building close working relationships with site leaders, ops managers, and delivery teams to weave practical WHS thinking into high-volume parcel handling, vehicle operations, manual handling, and last-mile delivery
  • Bringing proven experience leading operational work groups and managing a broad range of stakeholders
  • Advising and coaching business units on identifying and controlling risk — with particular focus on fatigue, traffic management, ergonomics, manual tasks, and contractor safety
  • Taking the lead on incident investigations and root cause analysis, driving corrective actions and championing a "learn and improve" approach

It's a workplace where the work genuinely matters, where safety maturity is taken seriously at every level, and where the pace and pressure reflect the importance of what's being delivered.

This means leading the end to end rewrite of procedures, standards, work instructions and supporting documentation, reviewing what currently exists and finding ways to simplify, standardise and modernise it, and translating technical and operational requirements into documentation people can actually use. It also involves facilitating consultation with operational teams, HSE professionals, subject matter experts and leadership through workshops, interviews and review sessions, owning the full document lifecycle from drafting through to consultation, review, approval, publication and periodic review, and coordinating document and version control so releases stay on schedule. The role supports internal and external audits relating to HSE systems and documentation, and requires ongoing monitoring of applicable HSE legislation and standards to keep everything current.

  • Translate technical and operational requirements into documentation that people can actually use

  • Own the full document lifecycle, from drafting through consultation, review, approval, publication and periodic review
  • Coordinate document and version control, tracking review comments, actions and approvals to keep releases on schedule
  • Support internal and external audits relating to HSE systems and documentation
  • Monitor applicable HSE legislation and standards, ensuring documentation reflects current obligations and best practice
THE ESSENTIALS
  • Demonstrated experience writing HSE procedures, standards, management system documentation or work instructions
  • Strong understanding of HSE management systems
  • Experience facilitating stakeholder consultation across operational and leadership levels
  • Excellent written communication, with the ability to simplify complex requirements for a broad audience
  • Strong project coordination and document management skills, with the ability to work independently

job.title: Health & Safety Business Partner - 4 month contact
job.description:
A national leader in manufacturing and production is looking to bring an experienced Health & Safety Advisor onto their operations team. This is an initial 4-month engagement with genuine scope to extend for the right person.
You'll be based on-site, embedded within a fast-paced industrial operation, working directly alongside the people who run it day to day. It's a role for someone who's happiest out on the floor rather than behind a desk — someone who can earn trust quickly, spot risk before it becomes a problem, and help shift safety from a compliance checkbox to something the whole team actually owns.
 
Please note, travel across NSW will be required from time to time. 

What you'll be doing
  • Acting as the go-to safety resource for site leaders, supervisors, and frontline crews
  • Getting out on the floor for inspections, audits, and risk assessments
  • Leading investigations into incidents and near misses, and following through on corrective actions
  • Helping embed and strengthen the site's Safety Management System
  • Running inductions, toolbox talks, and on-the-job training
  • Keeping the site aligned with WHS legislation and internal standards
  • Managing safety documentation and reporting with accuracy and rigor
  • Overseeing contractor safety compliance and permit-to-work processes
What you'll bring
  • A WHS Diploma or Degree, or equivalent hands-on experience
  • Runs on the board as a Health & Safety Advisor in manufacturing, industrial, or heavy operations environments
  • Strong grasp of WHS legislation and how safety management systems work in practice
  • Real experience leading incident investigations and risk assessments, not just reviewing them
  • The communication skills to influence everyone from machine operators to senior leaders
  • Comfortable owning your patch independently, while staying connected to the wider HSE team
  • A current driver's licence
To be considered for the role please 'apply' by submitting an up to date word version of your CV. For a confidential conversation please contact Matt on 0480 004 970.

job.title: Emergency Management Trainer
job.description:
Our client is a large and complex public health service organisation in Melbourne’s western suburbs, providing a broad range of services to a diverse and growing population. With a significant workforce operating across multiple sites and a wide range of clinical and non-clinical environments, the organisation is committed to maintaining a safe, resilient and well-prepared workplace.

This is an opportunity to join an organisation where emergency preparedness, business continuity and employee safety are critical to maintaining essential services and protecting patients, visitors and staff.

The Role
We are seeking an experienced Emergency Management Officer to support the organisation’s emergency preparedness, response and recovery capability. This role will have a strong focus on evacuation planning, emergency response procedures, exercising and employee training, ensuring people are well prepared to respond effectively to a range of emergency scenarios.

Working closely with operational teams and key stakeholders, you will help build a strong emergency management culture by developing practical plans, delivering engaging training and testing organisational readiness through exercises and simulations.
Key Responsibilities
  • Develop, review and maintain emergency management and evacuation plans across the organisation.
  • Conduct site assessments and identify opportunities to strengthen emergency preparedness and evacuation capability.
  • Develop and deliver emergency management, evacuation and emergency response training to employees, including Wardens and key emergency response personnel.
  • Develop and facilitate emergency exercises, drills and simulations to test organisational readiness and identify areas for improvement.
  • Provide guidance and support to employees and leaders regarding emergency response procedures, evacuation requirements and emergency roles and responsibilities.
  • Support the development and maintenance of Business Continuity and Emergency Management programs.
  • Review emergency management documentation, procedures and processes to ensure they remain current, practical and fit for purpose.
  • Assess emergency management capability and provide reports and recommendations to address identified gaps.
  • Coordinate emergency response activities and provide support during incidents and exercises where required.
  • Work collaboratively with stakeholders to promote a positive emergency preparedness and safety culture.
  • Maintain awareness of relevant legislation, standards and contemporary emergency management practices.
Essential Experience & Criteria
  • Relevant experience in emergency management, emergency planning, business continuity, risk management or a related field.
  • Demonstrated experience developing and reviewing evacuation and emergency response plans.
  • Proven experience delivering emergency management and evacuation training to employees and/or emergency response teams.
  • Experience developing and facilitating emergency exercises, drills and simulations.
  • Strong understanding of emergency management principles, risk assessment and organisational preparedness.
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively across all levels of an organisation.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to develop clear plans, procedures, reports and training materials.
  • Ability to identify gaps in emergency preparedness and develop practical, achievable recommendations.
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications in Emergency Management, Risk Management, Business Continuity, Occupational Health & Safety or a related discipline will be highly regarded.
What’s on Offer This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Emergency Management professional to play a key role in strengthening organisational preparedness, with a particular focus on evacuation planning, employee capability and emergency response training.

You will work with a broad range of stakeholders and have the opportunity to make a tangible impact on the organisation’s ability to prepare for and respond effectively to emergencies while supporting the delivery of essential community services.

How to apply 
For more information, please apply directly via the link with your resume. For additional inquiries, contact Jo Retallick at 0482 076 255 

Thank you for your interest, we look forward to receiving your application!
